entries.title: Genesis 19:1
segments: Two angels; according to the original, the two angels, namely, the two mentioned in the preceding chapter,
. Lot supposed them to be men.

entries.title: Genesis 19:5
segments: Though God bestow upon men a good land, and surround them with unnumbered mercies, if left without his grace they will grow worse and worse, till they become too wicked longer to live.

entries.title: Genesis 19:8
segments:
Bring them out; he esteemed the persons of his guests as sacred, and was willing to protect them at all costs.  But in this proposal he did very wrong, and showed the weakness of his faith in God. 
 
Of two natural evils, it is often proper to choose the least; but of two moral evils we should choose neither, and should never commit sin to avoid any supposed evil, or obtain any supposed good.  The only course of wisdom and safety is to trust in God and do right.

entries.title: Genesis 19:11
segments: All men are dependent upon God.  With him for their protector his people will be secure, and his enemies, in perseveringly opposing them, will be destroyed.

entries.title: Genesis 19:14
segments:
As one that mocked; they did not believe what he said. 
 
Faith in God is needful to salvation; and when he foretells the destruction of the wicked, if they do not believe him and escape, they will perish.

entries.title: Genesis 19:16
segments: God is more merciful to his people than they are to themselves; if he were not, they would all perish.

entries.title: Genesis 19:21
segments: From regard to one righteous man, though he be imperfect, God may save many from destruction.

entries.title: Genesis 19:22
segments:
I cannot do any thing; it was God's purpose to spare Lot and his family.  The work of destroying Sodom could not, therefore, be begun, till they had left the city. 
 
  Zoar; little.  It was called Zoar, as a memento of this event.  Its name before was Bela.

entries.title: Genesis 19:25
segments: Jehovah is a God of justice as well as mercy; and though he bear long with transgressors, if they turn not from their sins, he will in due time bring upon them overwhelming destruction.

entries.title: Genesis 19:26
segments: A pillar of salt; as a monument of the wrath of God against her for breaking his command.
One act of wilful disobedience to God may prove the occasion of immediate and irretrievable ruin.

entries.title: Genesis 19:27
segments: Where he stood; on the day before.

entries.title: Genesis 19:29
segments: It is a great blessing to have pious relatives, and to be the subject of their prayers.  From how many evils they have been and may be the means of saving us, none but God can tell.

entries.title: Genesis 19:32
segments:
The education of children amid scenes of gross depravity has a strong tendency to blunt their moral feelings.  They who needlessly expose their offspring to such a corrupting influence, cannot reasonably hope that they will walk in the ways of virtue. 
 
In solitude we are often more exposed to temptation, and in greater danger of complying with it, than in the crowded city; and the use of intoxicating drinks excites to the greatest abominations.

entries.title: Genesis 19:38
segments:
Ben-ammi; son of my people; that is, my kindred. 
 
  Ammon; the same as Ben-ammi.
